questions.question_text: Acidic chyme entering the duodenum must be neutralised before pancreatic enzymes work efficiently. Which secretion primarily supplies the required bicarbonate?
questions.option_a: Pancreatic juice
questions.option_b: Bile pigments
questions.explanation: Pancreatic juice contains bicarbonate ions that neutralise acidic chyme in the duodenum and provide a suitable pH for intestinal enzymes.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A person has had the gallbladder removed. Which statement about digestion remains correct?
questions.option_a: The liver continues to produce bile, though it is no longer stored and concentrated in the gallbladder
questions.option_b: Bile production shifts to the pancreas
questions.explanation: The liver produces bile; the gallbladder stores and concentrates it. Its removal does not stop bile production.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A child develops bloating and diarrhoea after drinking milk, while tolerating other foods. Which deficiency most directly explains this pattern?
questions.option_a: Lactase deficiency at the intestinal brush border
questions.option_b: Pepsin deficiency in the stomach
questions.option_d: Salivary amylase deficiency in the mouth
questions.explanation: Lactase splits lactose into absorbable monosaccharides. Undigested lactose can retain water and be fermented, causing symptoms of lactose intolerance.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Most absorbed long-chain fatty acids are reassembled in intestinal cells and leave the villi first through which route?
questions.option_a: Lacteals of the lymphatic system
questions.option_b: The hepatic portal vein directly as free fatty acids only
questions.explanation: Long-chain dietary fats are packaged into chylomicrons and enter lymphatic lacteals before reaching the bloodstream; many water-soluble nutrients enter blood capillaries directly.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A patient with severe diarrhoea loses large amounts of water and electrolytes. Which intestinal function has most directly failed to keep pace with fluid loss?
questions.option_a: Absorption of water and salts
questions.option_b: Secretion of bile pigments
questions.option_d: Filtration of blood in the kidneys
questions.explanation: The intestine normally absorbs water and electrolytes. Rapid transit and intestinal secretion during diarrhoea can exceed absorption, causing dehydration.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The stomach's muscular contractions mix food with gastric secretions. This mechanical action mainly helps by:
questions.option_a: Increasing contact between food and digestive juice to form chyme
questions.option_b: Absorbing most amino acids directly into the bloodstream
questions.option_d: Moving oxygen from lungs into blood
questions.explanation: Churning mechanically mixes food with gastric juice and forms semi-fluid chyme; most nutrient absorption occurs later in the small intestine.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which pancreatic enzyme-substrate pairing is correct?
questions.option_a: Trypsin—proteins and peptides
questions.option_b: Lipase—starch
questions.explanation: Trypsin is a protease acting on proteins and peptides in the small intestine; pancreatic lipase acts on fats and amylase on starch.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Why is trypsin released by the pancreas as inactive trypsinogen?
questions.option_a: To reduce the risk of autodigestion of pancreatic tissue
questions.option_b: To allow it to digest DNA in the nucleus
questions.option_c: Because it must first be stored in the gallbladder
questions.option_d: Because active trypsin cannot function in the small intestine
questions.explanation: Pancreatic proteases are secreted as inactive precursors; activation in the intestinal lumen helps protect the pancreas from self-digestion.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which pairing correctly identifies a major role of the liver in digestion and metabolism?
questions.option_a: Produces bile and converts excess amino-nitrogen to urea
questions.option_b: Stores urine and releases digestive enzymes
questions.explanation: The liver produces bile and also converts toxic ammonia generated during amino-acid metabolism into urea.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A meal rich in protein enters the stomach. Which event is required before pepsin can digest much of it?
questions.option_a: Pepsinogen is activated in the acidic gastric environment
questions.option_b: Bile salts convert pepsinogen into insulin
questions.option_c: Trypsin is secreted by the salivary glands
questions.explanation: Gastric hydrochloric acid helps convert inactive pepsinogen to pepsin, which then begins protein digestion in the stomach.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: The stomach lining is exposed to acid and protease yet is normally protected from extensive self-digestion. Which factor contributes most directly?
questions.option_a: A mucus-bicarbonate barrier over the epithelial lining
questions.option_b: A layer of bile inside the stomach
questions.option_c: A cellulose wall surrounding each stomach cell
questions.option_d: Continuous production of oxygen by gastric cells
questions.explanation: Mucus and bicarbonate help protect the gastric mucosa from acid and pepsin; disruption can contribute to injury and ulcers.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which statement best distinguishes digestion from absorption?
questions.option_a: Digestion breaks complex food into simpler molecules; absorption moves these products across the gut lining
questions.option_b: Digestion moves nutrients into blood; absorption breaks starch into sugars
questions.option_c: Both terms mean chewing food in the mouth
questions.option_d: Absorption occurs only in the oesophagus
questions.explanation: Digestion is chemical and mechanical breakdown of food; absorption is transfer of digested nutrients through the intestinal epithelium into blood or lymph.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A swallowed bolus is moved to the stomach even when a person is lying horizontally. Which mechanism explains this?
questions.option_a: Coordinated peristaltic contractions of the oesophagus
questions.option_b: Gravity alone pulling the bolus downward
questions.option_c: Ciliary beating in the stomach lining
questions.option_d: Diffusion of food through the oesophageal wall
questions.explanation: Peristaltic waves propel swallowed material along the oesophagus; transport does not depend solely on gravity.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: An infant's small intestine cannot efficiently split sucrose at its brush border. Which immediate consequence is most likely?
questions.option_a: Less glucose and fructose become available for absorption from sucrose
questions.option_b: Protein digestion in the stomach stops completely
questions.option_c: Bile production ceases in the liver
questions.explanation: Sucrase at the intestinal brush border hydrolyses sucrose into glucose and fructose, which can then be absorbed.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which digestive product is absorbed into blood capillaries of intestinal villi and carried first to the liver for processing?
questions.option_a: Many water-soluble nutrients such as glucose
questions.option_b: All long-chain fats as intact food droplets
questions.option_d: Bile salts only through the renal artery
questions.explanation: Monosaccharides and amino acids commonly enter villus blood capillaries and reach the liver through the hepatic portal circulation; long-chain fats primarily enter lymph first.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: After gastric mixing, chyme enters the duodenum through which muscular valve?
questions.option_a: Pyloric sphincter
questions.option_b: Ileocecal valve
questions.explanation: The pyloric sphincter controls passage of stomach contents into the duodenum and helps regulate gastric emptying.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A patient with damaged gastric mucosa cannot absorb vitamin B12 efficiently even though the ileum is intact. Which stomach secretion is most likely deficient?
questions.option_a: Intrinsic factor
questions.option_b: Bile salt
questions.explanation: Intrinsic factor, produced by gastric parietal cells, binds vitamin B12 and enables its absorption in the terminal ileum.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A fatty meal reaches the duodenum. Which hormone-mediated response helps coordinate its digestion?
questions.option_a: Cholecystokinin promotes gallbladder contraction and pancreatic enzyme secretion
questions.option_b: Gastrin closes the bile duct and stops pancreatic secretion
questions.option_c: Insulin releases pepsin into the stomach
questions.option_d: Thyroxine neutralises chyme in the duodenum
questions.explanation: Cholecystokinin released by the small-intestinal mucosa stimulates gallbladder contraction and pancreatic enzyme secretion.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which gastric hormone is released in response to food and promotes secretion of hydrochloric acid?
questions.option_a: Gastrin
questions.option_b: Secretin
questions.explanation: Gastrin from G cells stimulates gastric acid secretion and supports gastric motility.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which gastric-cell and secretion pairing is correct?
questions.option_a: Chief cell—pepsinogen
questions.option_b: Parietal cell—bile
questions.explanation: Chief cells secrete pepsinogen; parietal cells secrete hydrochloric acid and intrinsic factor.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: During swallowing, which structure helps prevent food from entering the airway?
questions.option_a: Epiglottis
questions.option_b: Uvula
questions.explanation: The epiglottis helps cover the laryngeal opening during swallowing, directing the bolus toward the oesophagus.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Which structure helps limit the backward movement of stomach contents into the oesophagus?
questions.option_a: Lower oesophageal sphincter
questions.option_b: Ileocecal valve
questions.explanation: The lower oesophageal sphincter helps reduce reflux of acidic stomach contents into the oesophagus.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: Humans obtain dietary fibre from cellulose mainly because they:
questions.option_a: lack enzymes that hydrolyse cellulose
questions.option_b: convert cellulose completely into glucose in the stomach
questions.explanation: Humans do not produce cellulase, so cellulose is not digested into glucose and contributes to dietary fibre.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: After a carbohydrate-rich meal, the liver removes some glucose from portal blood and stores it mainly as:
questions.option_a: Glycogen
questions.option_b: Cellulose
questions.explanation: The liver helps regulate blood glucose by converting some excess glucose to glycogen for storage.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php

questions.question_text: A broad-spectrum antibiotic course is followed by a temporary fall in vitamin K availability. Which explanation is most plausible?
questions.option_a: The normal intestinal microbiota contributes to vitamin K production
questions.option_b: The stomach normally converts vitamin K into bile
questions.option_c: The pancreas normally stores vitamin K in its islets
questions.option_d: The oesophagus normally synthesises vitamin K during swallowing
questions.explanation: Some intestinal bacteria synthesise vitamin K; disturbing the microbiota can reduce this contribution, although dietary sources also matter.
questions.source: Original SSC-level practice; factual reference: NCERT textbook portal https://ncert.nic.in/textbook.php
